description:
Resuming an interrupted campaign cell replays every previously completed sample through the decoder before producing one new sample, making continuation cost quadratic in the number of resumes.

## Background

The evaluator restores RNG position by iterating `simulate_frame` over the full recorded sample count. For a cell interrupted at 8M blocks the replay costs ~95 minutes of pure recomputation per additional invocation. Checkpointed evidence is durable, but continuation is only affordable when invocation bounds are chosen large enough to avoid resumes — the opposite of the bounded-run model campaign-resumability describes.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Resuming an interrupted cell reaches its first new sample in time independent of the completed-sample count (for example by persisting resumable RNG state), within the deterministic-seeded-execution contract.
- [hard] REQ-02: Resumed cells produce results identical to an uninterrupted run with the same seed and configuration.
- [hard] REQ-03: Existing committed checkpoints either remain readable or are refused with an explanatory schema-version error.
